original_question: Let F1 , F2 be Finsler metrics on a closed surface of genus ≥ 2.
target_in_paper: Question 10.1.3 in Section 10.1, "Metrics with integrable geodesic flow on surfaces of genus at least 2".
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the exact ambient setup of the paper’s Question 10.1.3: two Finsler metrics, F1 and F2, on a closed surface of genus at least 2. This matches the opening of the paper’s question almost verbatim.
missing_details: It does not name the common underlying surface M on which both F1 and F2 are defined.
It does not make explicit that the surface is closed, i.e. compact and without boundary.
It omits the crucial hypothesis: every unparameterized F1-geodesic is an F2-geodesic.
It does not explain what 'unparameterized' means here: the same geodesic curves up to reparameterization.
It omits the actual rigidity question being asked.
It does not specify that the desired conclusion is that F1 is obtained from F2 by scaling by a constant and adding a closed 1-form.
It does not specify that the scaling factor is a positive constant c > 0.
It does not specify that the added form is a closed 1-form beta on M, i.e. d beta = 0.
It does not spell out the formula on the tangent bundle: F1(x,v) = c F2(x,v) + beta_x(v) for all (x,v) in TM.
It does not indicate that this is posed in the paper as a special case of the Finsler version of the preceding higher-genus integrability/zero-Liouville-entropy discussion.
It does not preserve the paper’s asymmetric formulation: the hypothesis is about F1-geodesics being F2-geodesics, and the conclusion asks whether F1 must have the form c F2 + beta.
refined_question: Let M be a closed surface of genus at least 2, and let F1,F2: TM -> [0,∞) be Finsler metrics on M. Suppose that every F1-geodesic, considered as an unparameterized curve in M, is also an F2-geodesic. Must there exist a constant c > 0 and a closed 1-form beta on M such that F1(x,v) = c F2(x,v) + beta_x(v) for every (x,v) in TM?
justification: The draft is clearly aiming at Question 10.1.3, not a broader neighboring problem: the paper’s exact question begins with the same setup, 'Let F1, F2 be Finsler metrics on a closed surface of genus at least 2.' The nearby context in Section 10.1 says that this is 'a special case of the Finsler version' of the preceding question about zero Liouville entropy, and the sentence immediately after Question 10.1.3 explains why the question belongs in the integrability section: the second metric can be used to construct an integral of the geodesic flow of the first, while the Riemannian analogue is already known. The later discussion in Section 12 clarifies the relevant meaning of geodesics 'considered as unparameterized curves.'
